asOf: Updated Tue 22 Sep 2026, 09:15 Dubai · prices from 2026-09-21 close · for the Tue 22 Sep session
kicker: Dubai desk · US open 5:30pm Dubai (9:30am ET)
notes: Fed hiked rates 25bp to 3.75%-4% on Sept 16 (first hike since 2023) and signaled at least one more hike this year, keeping Chair Warsh focused on inflation over growth.
Wall Street just posted its best session since early August: S&P 500 +1.49% and Nasdaq Composite +2.26% to a record close, led by an AI-stock rally (AMD topped $1T market cap, Intel +12%, Meta +11%).

Oil has fallen for four straight sessions (Brent near $100, WTI ~$95.5) on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation and record Hormuz oil/LNG flows, even as the broader 2026 Iran war keeps crude well above pre-war levels.
Bitcoin spiked above $86,000 on a cascade of short covering (>$300M in shorts liquidated) as risk appetite improved alongside falling oil and yields.
Trump-Xi summit at the White House on Sept 24 is the week's biggest macro event, aiming to extend the Busan trade truce (tariffs, rare earths, soybeans, Taiwan arms, AI safety all on the table).
Quarter-end 'window dressing' flows and a dollar index at six-week highs post-Fed add to potential intraday volatility this week.
calendar: Tue Sep 22 (today): AutoZone (AZO), THOR Industries (THO) and MillerKnoll report before the open; KB Home (KBH) and Worthington Enterprises report after the close.
Wed Sep 23: General Mills (GIS), Cintas (CTAS), Paychex (PAYX) and Cracker Barrel report before the open; Meta's Connect 2026 keynote (new AI glasses, 'Phoenix' MR device) at 4pm PT/7pm ET.

Thu Sep 24: Trump hosts Xi Jinping at the White House for a high-stakes trade/Taiwan/AI summit; Costco (COST) and Darden Restaurants (DRI) report; new home sales data; FDA advisory panel votes on Grail's Galleri multi-ca
Fri Sep 25: August durable goods orders and final University of Michigan consumer sentiment.
Mon Sep 28: Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) earnings.
US IPO calendar is quiet this week domestically; no major US listings are pricing, in contrast to a busy week of new issues in the Indian market.

avoid.reason: AutoZone reports fiscal Q4 earnings before today's open into a backdrop of recent same-store-sales slowdown and multiple analysts (Oppenheimer, Wells Fargo, Barclays, Citi) cutting price targets ahead of the print.
KB Home reports Q3 results after today's close with consensus EPS of $0.90 versus $1.61 a year ago, and Wells Fargo maintains an Underweight rating into the print.
AMC Entertainment is on track to extend losses for a seventh straight trading day.
Lake Street downgraded Priority Technology Holdings to Hold and cut its price target from $13 to $8.05.
Sinclair's hostile takeover bid for Scripps was rejected, removing a key M&A catalyst for the stock.

items.name: Meta Platforms
items.news: Meta's new Muse AI agent has topped app-store charts and helped drive the stock's 11% single-day surge as investors position ahead of Meta's Sept 23-24 Connect keynote unveiling new AI glasses and a 'Phoenix' mixed-reality device. Citi has reiterated a Buy rating, citing bullishness on the AI glasses strategy following early hands-on demos.
items.risk: Stock has already run up sharply into the event, raising 'sell-the-news' risk if the hardware reveal underwhelms.
items.entry: Dip to $727.58–737.15, or break above $753.00 on volume

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices
items.news: AMD topped a $1 trillion market cap as Meta's Muse app fueled the AI-chip trade broadening beyond Nvidia, with hedge-fund ownership of the name rising through Q2. AMD has posted record data-center revenue this year on the back of its OpenAI and Anthropic GPU deals.
items.risk: Valuation is extended after outsized 2026 gains, making the stock sensitive to any AI capex disappointment.
items.entry: Dip to $602.76–611.69, or break above $618.07 on volume

items.name: Intel Corp
items.news: Intel jumped 12% Monday to close at $121.78 on renewed enthusiasm for its foundry strategy, reports of SK Hynix partnership talks for its Ohio fab, and a Tigress Financial price-target hike to $145; a TipRanks report noted Intel currently has enough chip supply for only about half its clients.
items.risk: The stock has run from the high-$80s to over $120 in weeks, leaving it vulnerable to a sharp pullback on any semis-sector wobble.
items.entry: Dip to $118.51–120.80, or break above $124.73 on volume

items.name: Arm Holdings
items.news: Arm shares jumped alongside Intel as Meta's Muse AI agent app drove renewed interest in server-processor demand tied to the broader AI buildout.
items.risk: Move is tied to sentiment/momentum rather than company-specific news, so it can fade quickly if the AI-chip rally stalls.
items.entry: Dip to $314.07–320.25, or break above $324.67 on volume

items.name: Summit Therapeutics
items.news: Reports indicate the U.S. Treasury is drafting rules to protect pharmaceutical licensing deals with Chinese companies, which would mitigate geopolitical risk for Summit's lead cancer candidate in-licensed from Akeso ahead of a November 2026 FDA action date.
items.risk: Clinical/regulatory-stage biotech carries binary risk around any trial or FDA-timeline news.
items.entry: Dip to $16.36–16.74, or break above $18.47 on volume

items.name: Greenland Energy
items.news: Greenland Energy surged over 140% in premarket Monday after President Trump announced a security pact granting the U.S. permanent access on Greenland, with the deal expected to be formally signed during this week's UN General Assembly; investors are speculating on greater U.S.-backed resource development on the island.
items.risk: Extremely volatile, low-float speculative name that has already moved multiples higher on no confirmed commercial deal, making a sharp reversal likely.
items.entry: Dip to $2.76–2.84, or break above $3.39 on volume
